method.personalPlay: Run 1: a cold, complete 30-night game with real touch taps in a fresh Playwright WebKit context at 390x844, using the tools/phone harness on port 9562. I made every strategy choice from on-screen information and played through settlement. Final fortune was ¤105,991 (Canal Runner, ledger #1). Run 2: a fresh run in the same profile, so the guided tour no longer showed, played to night 10 with a deliberately different opening. Net worth was +¤908 at night 10, against −¤172 at night 10 in run 1.

firstImpressions: The title screen is atmospheric: a lantern-lit drowned skyline with floating lanterns and gold serif type. The new-voyage card gives the debt terms right away (¤6,000 at 6% a night, due night 10). A skippable 5-step coach covers the ledger, first trade, canals, services and the deadline. The market is readable at 390 px, with an icon, sparkline, price, % against usual, and a note naming a better observed port and the quote's age. The map is an illustrated node map in which each district has its own building art and danger pips.

tradeLog.info: The opening harbor circular showed every port, and the headline 'best run' banner was Rust Pearls → Saint Mire +68% (¤962), with a bulletin that Saint Mire would pay anything.
tradeLog.chosen: Bought 4 Rust Pearls at ¤571 and sailed to Saint Mire.
tradeLog.outcome: On arrival on night 2, Saint Mire pearls were ¤507 ('Surge easing'), a 47% drop. I sold for −¤256. The headline trade was a mean-reverting trap.

tradeLog.info: At Copperhook, eels were ¤1,197 (−50% glut) and Saint Mire showed +114% two nights ago. The Glowkelp fleet call was +40%. My purse could not afford a single eel.
tradeLog.chosen: Sold kelp into the fleet call (+¤240) and 8 Bottled Rain, then bought 2 eels.
tradeLog.runnerUp: Keep 10 rain for the Saint Mire fleet call (N5-8) and buy 1 eel.
tradeLog.outcome: Tidewardens stopped me. Four failed runs took hull from 100% to 46%, then I hove to and lost 1 eel and 1 rain. The remaining eel sold for +¤648. Cash, not hold, was the binding constraint.

tradeLog.info: Debt was ¤9,565, due night 10, then 10% a night. After selling saffron (+¤1,528) and delivering a courier parcel (+¤3,040), the purse was ¤9,528.
tradeLog.chosen: Repaid 75% (¤7,146) and kept ¤2,382 as trading capital.
tradeLog.runnerUp: Repay everything, leaving ¤0 purse and ¤37 debt.
tradeLog.outcome: There was a real tension between debt and capital. The leftover ¤2.4k debt then compounded at 10% to ¤5,828, which I repaid on night 19.

tradeLog.info: Saint Mire saffron was ¤826 (−25%), and the public fleet calendar had a Synth Saffron call at Fogmouth for N13-16, one night away at risk 4/5.
tradeLog.chosen: Bought 6 saffron and sailed to Fogmouth.
tradeLog.runnerUp: Go to Lanternquay to repay the 10% debt and repair.
tradeLog.outcome: Tidewardens again. The bribe of ¤1,336 was just above my ¤1,240 purse, so I hove to and lost 3 of 6. The 3 left sold at ¤3,272 each (+¤7,338).

tradeLog.info: At the Sluices, Dreamsilk finally had dealers at ¤12,280 after three ports showed none, and the eel fleet call at the Exchange ran N17-20.
tradeLog.chosen: Sold 2 silk (+¤15,322), patched to 75% for ¤464, bought 10 eels and 10 pearls, and sailed to the Exchange.
tradeLog.runnerUp: Moon Ink at ¤18,174 for Lanternquay at +52%.

tradeLog.info: The purse held ¤38.1k. The ¤6,000 wireless was available.
tradeLog.chosen: Bought the wireless and 3 Dreamsilk at ¤8,761 for Lanternquay, where the live quote was ¤13.0k.
tradeLog.runnerUp: Keep the ¤6k and run the eel loop again.
tradeLog.outcome: On arrival, the Lanternquay silk quote of ¤13.0k had become ¤10,943 (−16%). Even live quotes decay sharply overnight.

tradeLog.info: On night 20, Copperhook silk showed ¤21,681 'seen tonight' two nights away. Arriving on night 22, it was ¤6,716. Ghost chips were ¤8,505.
tradeLog.chosen: Sold 2 chips (+¤6,970), fully repaired (¤875), bought 7 eels for the Exchange, and carried the silk to the Sluices.
tradeLog.outcome: The silk sold at the Sluices for ¤12,914 (+¤8,306). Racks were never worth buying, because hold was not binding once high-value goods were affordable.

tradeLog.info: The Exchange had saffron at ¤873, with the Sluices at +315% (¤3,619) one night away.
tradeLog.runnerUp: A silk-only run to the Lanternquay fleet call on N29-30.
tradeLog.outcome: A leak forced a ¤3,300 patch to save 5 saffron. The surge eased to ¤2,830, which with price impact gave +¤27,398 on 14 units plus +¤8,921 on 6.

tradeLog.info: Deadline next night. The purse held ¤79.6k and the Lanternquay vault was available. Moon Ink showed Orchid +24%, and pearls showed Exchange ¤605 and Orchid ¤498.
tradeLog.chosen: Deposited ¤60k, bought 24 pearls, and sailed to Orchid to sell the Moon Ink.
tradeLog.runnerUp: The Exchange with 29 pearls, selling the Moon Ink at Lanternquay.
tradeLog.outcome: Moon Ink sold for ¤24,736 (+¤6,562) and pearls +¤720. The vault paid ¤900. Settled at ¤105,991.

tradeLog.info: A different opening: saffron at ¤841 for Fogmouth +104%, and kelp for Copperhook at +84% during the fleet call. The fleet calendar was identical to run 1.
tradeLog.chosen: Avoided the run-1 surge trap and bought 2 saffron plus 18 kelp.
tradeLog.outcome: Fogmouth saffron arrived at ¤1,311 against a ¤1,715 quote, so I carried it on and sold at Copperhook for ¤1,035. Kelp gained +¤594 in the fleet call.

tradeLog.info: From run 1, I knew the Bottled Rain fleet call at Saint Mire runs N5-8.
tradeLog.chosen: Bought 21 rain at Copperhook for Saint Mire on night 5.
tradeLog.runnerUp: Saint Mire saffron for the later Fogmouth call.
tradeLog.outcome: I tested Fight (two misses, −16% and −13% hull) and a failed run, then hove to and lost 10. Nine rain sold at ¤236. On night 6 Lanternquay had no rain dealers, so I adapted to an eel trade (+¤914), a parcel job and the Orchid pearl fleet call (+¤2,178).

observations: C1 Trade: Nearly every logged turn had a credible runner-up, including the closing turn on night 29 (Orchid against the Exchange, and vault against carrying cash). Changes in cash, capacity and deadline changed the right choice: night 4 cash shortfall ('You can't afford even one'), night 7 reserve against leak-patch money, night 29 deadline. Trade-sheet tools make quantity a decision: a 15% reserve default, Max with price impact, dealer depth ('Dealers here sell about 24 more at this price'), a profit preview, and a warning 'Above the best observed sale price ... Buy fewer'.

C1 counterevidence: After about night 12, hold capacity rarely bound in my run. Dealer depth and cash bound instead, and I never filled 30 hold with high-value goods. The trade sheet opens in Sell mode when you hold the good (keydown line 1817 and touch). On night 28 a scripted buy of 4 Dreamsilk became a −¤698 sale of my 2. That was partly my unverified scripted tap, but the risk is real.

C2 Routes: The map has lit 1-night canals, 2-night waypoint routes that let you trade at the waypoint, danger pips and numeric risk (1/5 to 4/5), Port details with dated quotes per good, district supply/import habits, and a public fleet calendar. The whisper and the wireless are two information upgrades.

C2 observations against arrivals: Saint Mire pearls ¤962 on night 1 became ¤507 on arrival (−47%). Copperhook kelp went ¤44 to ¤61 under the fleet call (as signalled). Saint Mire pearls ¤490 became ¤347. Before buying information, I paid ¤340 for a whisper on night 10 ('likely; half land in full; 1 in 5 turns'), and it landed: eels went to ¤781 (−67%) and I made +¤4,144. After buying the wireless: Lanternquay silk ¤13.0k became ¤10,943 (−16%), and Copperhook silk '¤21,681 seen tonight' on night 20 was ¤6,716 on night 22 (−69%). In run 2, Fogmouth saffron ¤1,715 became ¤1,311, and Lanternquay pearls ¤439 became ¤356.

C2 counterevidence: Quote reliability is explained only in words ('may change'). The magnitude of overnight decay is large and not shown. The night-1 headline 'best run' pointed at a surge that collapsed. Map and banner '+%' badges are relative to different bases (cargo cost against local price), which confused me twice. A 2-night route picks its own waypoint, though stopping at the waypoint and choosing again works.

C3 Economy: The debt is 6% a night to night 10, then 10%. After repayment, credit of ¤30,000 opens. The vault pays 1.5% (verified: ¤60,000 to ¤60,900). Upgrades are hold racks (¤2,500, or ¤2,920 to ¤4,720 from Old Fenna's offers), a twin-screw motor (¤4,500), a wireless set (¤6,000), flare pistols (¤2,500 or ¤3,000), ¤20,000 charters, whispers (¤300 + 1.5% of assets), a full repair (¤35 a point) and a Gutter Yard patch to 75% (¤16 a point). Debt against capital was a real decision on night 9.

C3 counterevidence: I did not test borrowing the ¤30k credit, charters, racks, engine or weapons in personal play, so I have no equivalent-state shortcut check. Racks looked dominated once high-value goods were affordable. The public fleet calendar was identical in both runs, so a memorized loop (Saint Mire saffron to Fogmouth N13-16, eels to the Exchange N17-20, silk at Orchid N25-28 and Lanternquay N29-30) is a strong repeatable plan. It still needs trading, so it is not a bypass. Bot fortunes ranged from ¤81.7k to ¤619k, which suggests high variance.

C4 Risk: Encounters state their odds and stakes: 'Run 37% each try ... rakes hull and grab 12%', 'Fight 22% per volley; 60% they hit back', 'Bribe ¤4,883 Guaranteed', 'Heave to: seize half'. Outcomes matched: heave-to took exactly half (rounded up). The bribe deducted exactly ¤4,883 (¤13,727 to ¤8,844). Squall 'push through, lose 6 to 16%' cost −8%. Flotsam '4 in 5' gave 11 kelp. The whisper landed as described.

C4 recovery: After the night-4 hit (hull 46%, cargo seized), recovery options were the parcel job (+¤3,040), the leak patch or jettison, the Gutter Yard cheap patch, and a Copperhook repair. Each had a meaningful cost. A ¤3,300 leak patch on night 27 saved about ¤18k of saffron.

C4 counterevidence: The Gull Gang toll copy says 'About a fifth of your purse plus a cut of your cargo', but on night 8 it charged ¤683 of an ¤859 purse (80%) and took no cargo. The bribe was priced just above my purse three times when I was poor (¤878 against ¤146, ¤1,336 against ¤1,240, ¤750 against ¤584). The Boathook fight is weak (two misses for −29% hull in run 2). I sailed nights 4 to 17 at 46% hull because I did not know about the Gutter Yard. The directory lists it, but no low-hull prompt points to it.

C5 Pacing: The opening is shaped by the night-10 debt deadline and small capital. Growth runs on fleet-call loops and upgrades (wireless, repair, vault). The closing has a 'Final night! Sell your cargo, then settle up' banner, the Lanternquay silk fleet call on N29-30, and my night-29 vault and route decision. Every night had a meaningful choice. The ending reconciles: cash ¤45,091 + vault ¤60,900 = ¤105,991. Interest accrued ¤6,974 equals ¤12,974 repaid minus ¤6,000 principal. Encounters 5 / fled 1 match my log, and the screen says '¤144,009 short of Lantern Broker'.

C5 counterevidence: Nights 14-16 were mostly spent carrying Dreamsilk that had no dealers at Saint Mire, Orchid or the Exchange. Choices still existed, but they felt forced. The 'Interest accrued' label does not say it is debt interest.

C6 Replay: Run 2 had different prices, events (Pell's rumour, flotsam, strongbox ¤950) and a different opening. I changed my early plan (saffron and kelp instead of the pearl surge, rain bought for the fleet call) and my later plan (no rain dealers at Lanternquay on night 6, so eels, a parcel job and the Orchid pearl fleet call). The map, districts, habits and the whole fleet calendar were identical across runs. Approaches worth trying next: buying information early (wireless plus whispers), a charter at one district, and borrowing the ¤30k credit for the N13-16 saffron call.

C7 Onboarding: The coach covers ledger, trade, canals, services and deadline. The handbook covers price colours, reserve, impact, debt rates and danger. Arrival tips appear in the log. Sheet messages explain constraints ('You can't afford even one', 'Uses your 15% reserve', 'A big order moves the price: past 10 ...') and unexpected prices ('Surge easing', 'Glut', 'No dealers tonight'). After the opening, I made reasoned choices without lookups.

C7 counterevidence: The night-1 headline route taught the wrong lesson. Before repaying, the consequences of late debt and collectors are not stated beyond the rate. The Gutter Yard was not surfaced when hull was low. '+%' bases differ between surfaces. The message 'Price today is about usual' appears for a good with no dealers.

C8 Input: Touch reached settlement at 390x844 in WebKit. The phone audit on market and map found 0 targets under 44 px, 0 text contrast under 4.5:1 (approximate), 0 inputs under 16 px and no horizontal overflow. At 1280 px Chromium, the keyboard reached title, trade sheet (Arrow/Enter/B, Tab to the confirm button), map (Tab to node, or digit keys), sail, the Escape menu, settlement and the ending, each with a 2px amber focus outline on buttons and rows. The official keyboard runner completed 30 nights with 0 pointer events. Mouse select-and-sail worked, and M toggles mute and persists it. Non-colour cues include signed %, 'Cheap'/'Pricey' chips and counted danger pips. A prefers-reduced-motion rule is present (39 running animations against 58 at 800 ms).

C8 counterevidence: Map nodes show focus only by thickening the disc stroke (outline:none), which is hard to see. After Tab+Enter on a node, focus moves to Close rather than Sail, so a second Enter closes the card even though Sail shows a ⏎ hint (desk2.cjs: night 2 stayed night 2). I did not personally check event-modal focus or contrast at 1280 px. All touch was emulated in Playwright WebKit on Windows: no real iOS, safe areas or on-screen keyboard.

C9 World: Districts are recognizable by art and writing (lighthouse Fogmouth, crane Copperhook, sunken cathedral Saint Mire, pumps at the Sluices, a columned Exchange, hanging gardens at Orchid) with flavour lines ('A cathedral sunk to its belfry...'). I could follow buy, voyage and encounter without the log. Buy shows a toast 'Loaded 4 Rust Pearls for ¤2,284' and a purse count-down. A voyage shows the skiff on the map and a 'NIGHT 25 OF 30' card. An encounter has an illustrated searchlight scene and a per-try result line. The ending has a rank emblem, breakdown and ledger.

C9 sound: The source has 18 distinct synthesized cues (buy, sell, profit, travel, arrive, event, alarm, hit, shot, escape, win, lose, upgrade, splash, bank and others) plus canal ambience. Under the iOS-policy stand-in, the AudioContext was created in a touchend and resumed there, with 10 sounds started while running and 0 while suspended. Mute works by button and the M key. Listening quality was not judged because Playwright Windows WebKit has no Web Audio.

C9 counterevidence: In headless WebKit, a voyage plus night card took about 6-7 s per hop (the harness notes rAF runs at about 4 per second). I could not judge normal-device pace beyond the Chromium automation. Some toasts vanish quickly ('Read' was gone before I could tap it).

C10 Reliability: The game booted from file://. The ledger survived a reload (¤105,991 Canal Runner). The phone harness showed no errors after the reload nav. verify.cjs passed corrupt-storage recovery, a sandbox with storage blocked and the game starting, 0 network requests, and the size and syntax check (253,939 bytes). All localStorage access is wrapped in try/catch with an in-memory fallback. The only http string is the SVG xmlns in a data: favicon. NOTES.md is 59 lines. My spot arithmetic checks all held: 4×571=2,284, the bribe deduction, vault interest and the ending sum.

C10 counterevidence: I did not capture page errors during my personal run 1, because the harness error log resets on nav and I checked only after the reload. Error-free full runs come from the automated runners (errors: []).
limits: Touch was Playwright WebKit on Windows with emulated touch at 390x844 and dpr 3. Real iOS Safari, safe-area insets, toolbars, the on-screen keyboard and audible audio were not tested.
Audio was judged from source and the harness's iOS-policy AudioContext stand-in only. No sound was heard.

The run-1 personal play used scripted harness taps that I chose step by step. Three unintended actions were harness errors, not game defects. On night 2 a nav tap landed on an 'Abandon' row, and the confirm dialog caught it. On night 20 a nav tap landed under an open modal and declined a courier job. On night 23 a nav tap hit 'Shelter' and cost a night.
On night 28 a scripted 'buy 4' landed in a Sell-mode sheet and sold 2 silk. It is recorded as a UX risk, but the trigger was my unverified tap.
Run 2 was played in the same browser profile after run 1, so the guided tour did not repeat. It stopped at night 10 per protocol.
Not personally tested: borrowing credit, charters, racks, engine, weapons, sinking, Fogmouth weapons, external keyboard on phone, screen readers, and contrast or focus on event modals at 1280.

The automated runners are the organizer's shared harness scripts, re-run by me into private output directories. They use FAST timing and reduced motion, and their event checks use explicit fixture states.
No change history, other judges' reports, or other judging files were read. judging/trading-research.md showed as modified in git status by someone else and was not read.
priorities: Make price-signal reliability visible and stop headlining surges. Show each quote's expected overnight drift or a confidence band by age and volatility, and mark surge-driven prices as likely to fade. The night-1 'best run' (pearls ¤962) collapsed to ¤507, and a 'seen tonight' wireless quote of ¤21.7k was ¤6.7k two nights later. Players should be able to tell signal from noise without being burned.

Align encounter copy with outcomes and surface recovery. The Gull Gang toll says 'a fifth of your purse plus a cut of cargo' but took 80% of the purse and no cargo. Bribes kept landing just above a poor captain's purse. Add a low-hull prompt naming the Gutter Yard patch and the Copperhook repair, because I sailed 13 nights at 46% hull unaware. Spell out what happens if Marrow is not paid by night 10.

Remove input traps in the trade and map flows. Keep the trade sheet in the player's last-used mode, or make Sell-mode entry unmistakable (it cost a −¤698 unintended sale). After Enter on a map node, focus Sail, which carries the ⏎ hint, not Close, and give nodes a visible focus ring. Separately, give hold capacity late-game relevance, such as depth-linked or bulk-good incentives, because racks were never worth buying once high-value goods unlocked.
